extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark for evaluating large multimodal models’ ability to detect self-contradictory or conflicting instructions across language-language and vision-language settings. It contains 20,000 conflicts and includes multiple task types and dataset splits.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created using the AutoCreate framework, which starts from manually input seeds and then automatically generates data through a generator-decorator-cleaner pipeline, with human experts and LLMs double-checking quality. For SemanticConflict, the process additionally uses ImageNet images and substitutes labels in questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consisted of manually provided seed examples, generated language and vision data, and for SemanticConflict, images retrieved from ImageNet.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts manually checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset; the dataset was also refined through a generator-decorator-cleaner pipeline with 'both human experts and LLMs' involved in double-checking quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality was checked by human experts and double-checked with LLMs; the paper says the dataset was rigorously checked for quality, but does not report agreement metrics.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large language models (LLMs) were used in the automatic dataset creation framework (AutoCreate) to generate and decorate data, and to double-check quality.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark currently only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms, which may bias evaluation toward these modalities and away from others.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited to language-language and vision-language settings, does not provide fine-grained control over conflict degree, and does not include a detailed study of attention mechanisms under conflicting instructions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work is intended to help researchers and practitioners assess and improve multimodal models' ability to handle conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction, communication technologies, inclusivity in AI research, and trust and reliability in AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The SCI benchmark is used for evaluating large multimodal models on detecting conflicting commands; it serves as a standardized platform for assessment and improvement, and the AutoCreate framework supports creation of diverse instruction datasets.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset includes post-processing modifications such as changing numerical data to the maximum/minimum value, substituting correct labels with similar but different objects, and selecting manual subsets (SCI-Base and SCI-Core) from SCI-All.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data are generated through an automatic pipeline with generator-decorator-cleaner steps, including cleaning by a cleaner that removes data not meeting quality standards and human/LLM quality checks.
